title: Pocket Casts

components.caption: A settings screen assembled from this module's own app bar, sections and rows — the surface pattern most Pocket Casts screens follow.
Account screen: subscription rows over a primary action and a destructive outlined action. Dark is where the destructive support05 label and border have the least contrast to work with.
The filled full-width action button — the primary call to action on almost every Pocket Casts sheet.
The secondary full-width action — a border and a tinted label rather than a fill.
The lowest-emphasis full-width action: label only, no fill or border.
The filled action button with an in-place progress state, used where a tap kicks off a network call.
The gradient-filled action reserved for Plus and Patron upgrade paths.
The full-width dismiss action at the foot of a sheet.
The round filled button used for compact single-action affordances.
A round icon button on a tinted circle.
The bare close affordance used in sheet and dialog corners.
The 32dp icon button with an unbounded ripple — the compact tap target used inside rows and toolbars. Previewed across all nine palettes.
The bordered segmented icon group behind the podcasts-layout and filter pickers, across all nine palettes. Its selected cell inverts to primaryInteractive02 on a primaryInteractive01 fill.
The pill tab row used to switch between list scopes.
The play affordance that doubles as a duration/remaining-time label, across all nine palettes.
The standard single-line text field used across sign-in and naming flows.
The paired email and password fields with their reveal toggle — the sign-in form.
The search field in its default and small styles, filled and empty, across all nine palettes.
Minus/value/plus stepper, used for skip intervals and episode limits.
The segmented control used to switch between two or three peer views.
A single-select option list with a checked row, across all nine palettes.
The folder colour swatch picker with its selection ring.
The whole H10–P60 type ramp in one sheet — the sizes, weights and colours every other component draws from.
Clamped description text with its show-more affordance.
Text that shrinks to fit a fixed box rather than wrapping or ellipsising.
The 'n podcasts selected' summary line.
The explicit-content badge at its default and two alternative tints, across all nine palettes.
Playlist artwork built from a single episode's cover.
A folder's tinted cover grid.
A podcast list row with its inline subscribe toggle, across all nine palettes.
The multi-select podcast list used when scoping a filter.
A bookmark list row: title, timestamp and play affordance, across all nine palettes.
The inline dismissible banner used for tips and upsell nudges, across all nine palettes.
The empty-state banner — icon, title, subtitle and up to two actions, across all nine palettes.
The standard confirm/dismiss dialog, across all nine palettes.
The coach-mark tooltip with its pointer, across all nine palettes.
The sparkle treatment used to celebrate an upgrade or a completed action, across all nine palettes.
The themed top app bar in its solid and immersive styles, across all nine palettes. Its secondaryUi01 background against the content's primaryUi01 is the pairing most worth checking per theme.
The app bar used at the head of a modal sheet, with a close affordance.
The full modal sheet body — title, copy and stacked actions, across all nine palettes.
The paging dots used under onboarding and end-of-year carousels.
The list divider — the thinnest thing in the system, and the one most likely to vanish on a low-contrast palette.
A drag-to-reorder action row, as used when customising the player's action bar.
The workhorse settings row: primary text, optional secondary text, optional icon and optional toggle.
A titled group of setting rows with its divider, across all nine palettes.
The explanatory row that sits under a setting to describe what it does.
The profile avatar with its subscription ring, across all nine palettes.
The Plus badge in its coloured treatment across light and dark surfaces.
The roundel on its own.
Roundel and wordmark side by side, the lockup used in app bars.
The stacked lockup used on splash and sign-in surfaces.
The branded attribution pill stamped onto shared images.
The numeric badge at its medium size.
An icon filled with the Plus gradient rather than a flat tint.
